finnhub-141124058.headline: What’s the ‘Ceiling’ on How Much Microsoft, Amazon, and Google Can Spend on AI?
finnhub-141124058.summary: In this segment of the AI Investor Podcast from 24/7 Wall St., Eric Bleeker lays out his framework for evaluating the AI trade, describing it as a stool resting on three legs: technological progress, real-world adoption, and the ability to finance the buildout. Two legs he considers extremely strong. On progress, he points to Nvidia's backing of a straight-shot superintelligence effort, ongoing gains in training and model capability, and expectations of highly capable autonomous models at roughly human level, at scale, within a year. On adoption, he cites OpenAI's monthly revenue now exceeding its prior full quarter, Microsoft noting that 90% of cloud demand comes from outside the frontier labs, and Google's 82% cloud growth. Adoption is uneven, concentrated among a relatively small group of heavy users, but strong. Financing is the weak leg and the source of most current fear. Bleeker estimates $700 to $800 billion in AI data center spending this year, growing to roughly $1.2 trillion next year, against a financing ceiling he places somewhere between $1.5 and $2 trillion annually. With 2028 expectations near $1.4 trillion, the market is approaching that ceiling, which is why valuation now dominates stock selection. A company historically worth 15 times earnings trading at 40 times its 2028 or 2029 numbers is hard to defend. He closes with three points: the selloff is likely closer to its end than its beginning, macro risks remain including a possible September rate rise and soft GDP, and for anyone sidelined by prior valuations, this is arguably the most attractive entry point since spring 2025.
finnhub-141124058.reason: 探討AI支出上限，影響未來成長。

The site in the port city of Visakhapatnam, also known as Vizag, it sits near forests, reservoirs, and wildlife sanctuary buffers on in a city that is already facing water shortages. Activists, they say clearances were fast-tracked without assessing the impact on the city's water supply or on local wildlife. "The city has already seen at least five street marches, also some round table discussions around the concerns of this project. There have been at least four cases, including in the state's top court, as well as the environmental tribunal in India, all asking for the project work to be halted because of the environmental concerns.""Google has given us a very detailed statement for the story saying the project will be complying with all applicable laws on water. They say they will use air cooling technology in the data center facility, which will significantly reduce the water usage.""On the wildlife concerns, Google says in their words, they're going to be a silent neighbor because they're gonna use sound dampening fans as well as landscape buffers.""The state of Andhra Pradesh has responded to Reuters in a statement. They have said that the concerns of activists are incorrect and misleading, but said that they are open to feedback. They have added that the protesters have every right to protest. And it is open to corrections if it finds that there is any legitimacy to the claims."
